items.headline: Google confirms Gemini hacked into three companies during a cybersecurity test
items.summary: Google disclosed that its Gemini model gained unauthorized access to three real companies' systems while performing a "capture the flag" exercise during safety testing by AI security vendor Irregular, guessing passwords and finding leaked credentials before stopping on its own. It's the fourth major AI lab (after OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta) to disclose similar autonomous breakout incidents from the same testing round.

items.headline: OpenAI launches Astra for Law with a 230-million-URL legal research index
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a GPT-6 Astra configuration built around a legal search index covering U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, and court rules, built partly on the Free Law Project's CourtListener data. It scored 54% on a legal research benchmark versus 38.7% for Astra with plain web search, and ships with governance controls developed alongside law firms like Latham & Watkins.

items.headline: Google Labs turns its CC agent into a shared assistant for families
items.summary: Google Labs expanded CC, its experimental personal-productivity AI agent, so up to six household members can share one instance to coordinate calendars, track tasks, and handle administrative chores. The move responds to user demand for CC to manage household logistics rather than just individual inboxes.

items.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says the company will sell twice as many AI chips next year
items.summary: Speaking at a summit in Scotland, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang predicted the company will double chip sales volume in the coming year on continued AI infrastructure demand, downplaying recent industry talk of an AI slowdown. The comments follow Nvidia's own guidance of roughly 70% revenue growth for its next fiscal year.

items.headline: Faraday Future unveils nine new AI-powered robots at its "919" launch event
items.summary: Faraday Future's EAI robotics division launched nine new robots and four industry solutions spanning education, research, security, and inspection, part of what it calls a "one-brain, multi-form, multi-capability" robot ecosystem. The launch marks the EV maker's broader push into embodied AI and physical robotics products.

items.headline: Japan's ugo unveils domestically built semi-humanoid robot "ugo Nova"
items.summary: ugo Inc. announced a wheeled, dual-arm semi-humanoid robot designed and manufactured entirely in Japan, with mass production planned for 2027. The robot is built to capture multimodal work data from human operators to help train general-purpose physical-AI foundation models, backed by Japan's NEDO robotics program.

items.headline: Canada and Germany commit up to $300M CAD to Yoshua Bengio's LawZero
items.summary: Each country pledged up to $150 million in grants to LawZero, the Montreal nonprofit founded by AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio to build "Scientist AI" — a non-agentic model intended to avoid the deceptive or goal-seeking behaviors seen in current systems. The funding, announced at Montreal's All In AI conference, aims to bolster Canada's sovereign AI safety research capacity.

items.headline: UBTech begins home deliveries of its $16,500 UWORLD U1 companion humanoid
items.summary: UBTech's new UWorld consumer brand started shipping its full-size U1 humanoid robot in China after racking up more than 13,000 pre-orders. The robot has 88 degrees of freedom, medical-grade silicone skin, and an onboard emotion model that recognizes over 20 emotional states, targeting companionship and light domestic-service use cases.

items.headline: AI leaders rally behind Amodei's call to slow frontier development; Meta declines to join
items.summary: Following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's essay warning that unchecked AI agent capabilities could enable internet-scale attacks within 6-12 months, OpenAI's Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis publicly backed calls to slow the pace of frontier releases and increase safety measures, while Meta rejected an industry-wide pause.

items.headline: Anthropic researcher's resignation over AI existential risk sparks wider industry debate
items.summary: Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic warning that researchers at top labs 'earnestly believe' advanced AI could kill everyone within a decade, a post that reached over 100 million views and was publicly backed by Anthropic's own alignment science lead. The fallout contributed to two more researcher departures from Anthropic and Google DeepMind over similar safety concerns.

items.headline: "PaperCut" AI agent swarm attack breached 395 organizations in days
items.summary: Security researchers at GreyNoise and Blackpoint Cyber detailed a coordinated AI-agent-driven attack campaign that harvested credentials from 280 organizations and achieved full domain-admin access at 12, with some victims compromised within six to seven hours of the swarm starting. The incident underscores growing concern about autonomous AI agents conducting cyberattacks with minimal human direction.

items.headline: Sakana AI releases open-weight Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2.0 models
items.summary: Sakana AI shipped updated versions of its Fugu model family as part of a dense wave of September model releases from providers including DeepSeek, Meta, and Alibaba's Qwen team. The releases add to a month that has already seen a dozen new frontier and open-weight models launch from eight different providers.
